title: The collective poem behind «Хищные грибы Узбекистана»
scope: A documented literary afterlife of a real scientific title. Dates below establish circulation, not an unverified date of invention.

sources.title: Хищные грибы Узбекистана. Почти бесконечная песнь
sources.evidence: The dated post describes itself as preserving a collective social-media contribution and prints an extended sequence of stanzas. It points to a Facebook post as its source. Bezuglov is the republisher, not established as sole author.
sources.limit: The upstream Facebook post was not accessible. The full contributor list, first stanza author and first publication date were not established.

sources.title: Repost in the «Анекдот» thread
sources.evidence: A post dated 15 October 2023 repeats the collective poem and links to the 2018 blog and the Facebook source.
sources.limit: The thread itself began in 2010. Its 2010 thread date must not be used to date this poem.

sources.title: Сага о хищных грибах Узбекистана
sources.evidence: A later compilation explicitly makes the poetry central and links to several branches and mirrors.
sources.limit: The poster's account of origins is not independent proof of a first author. Its quoted fantastical account of ancient man-eating fungi is not accepted as Uzbek folklore or biology.

interpretation.form: An open-ended, multi-voice sequence, predominantly quatrains, repeatedly returning to the title as a refrain. Rhyme around «Узбекистана» acts as a constraint that invites another stanza.
interpretation.registers: Mock epic, horror comedy, domestic absurdity, scientific and bureaucratic language, mythology and literary/pop-cultural allusions. Uneven metres and tonal collisions are part of its communal character.
interpretation.conceptual_link: My reading: the poem's branching, distributed authorship resembles a mycelium; the recurring rhyme works metaphorically like a trapping ring. This is an artistic interpretation, not a claim made by the biological papers.
interpretation.revised_direction: Give the phrase its chorus. Show a dry catalogue entry growing into a shared, unruly language-world. Use typography, repetition, and comic unease alongside the biology.
interpretation.cultural_caution: This is Russian-language internet verse about a place-name, not established Uzbek oral tradition. Do not treat its grotesque stereotypes or man-eating imagery as ethnographic fact.

reuse: Link to the existing poem and discuss its form. Do not reproduce the complete collective text or claim it as newly authored. The new poem at artwork/poem.txt is a separate original response.
